inbox.guide:
LANTERN / tabletop digital show — delivered contract
Three panels contain 8 combinational gates, 3 one-tick memories and 3 named lights: 14 modules. Follow the three illustrated sheets. The received inventory lists types, not wiring. A connector word is one signal everywhere, independent of arrow placement. Solid dots join; arched bridges do not join. All endpoints have a local pin label. Rotation changes the location of the local pin, not its meaning. Never infer pins from page left/right. Gates have a,b,out. MASK means a AND NOT b, not a symmetric gate. Memory has D, EN, Q. Lights copy their attached signal.
Finite model: bits only. OR=1 if either input; AND=1 only if both; XOR=1 only if different. Every gate has zero tick delay. Only MEM delays, always exactly one tick. There are no analog rules and no combinational cycles. No implicit inversion. EN is active high. At tick t: take old Q and that tick's Tap/Sweep; compute E0=(t even AND Allow even), E1=(t odd AND Allow odd); evaluate all combinational gates from that snapshot; render lights and report the complete row; finally commit all memory D values simultaneously wherever EN=1, otherwise retain old Q. next Q is state for t+1. A memory output in the same row is always old Q.
The horizon is ticks 0..11. Initial Q012 comes from the edition and is editable. A pulse occupies exactly its checked input frame, one tick, even if adjacent checks form a longer high. Missing input frames are zero. Zero input is not an implicit reset: existing memories still evolve. Playback starts paused at tick 0. Step advances to the next row, capped at 11. Back and scrub recompute from saved/draft initial state, never reverse a physical update. Play advances at the edition rate and stops at 11; Pause freezes the row. Rate changes display speed only.
Edit sequence opens a draft for pulses, Allow even/odd, initial bits and edition notes. Draft changes immediately recompute all 12 rows and the preview. Undo reverses one draft operation. Cancel restores the saved edition. Save commits all editable data. Reload retains saved data, not an abandoned draft. Reset edition restores only the selected edition's delivered defaults (including note and initial bits); the other edition is untouched.
The live display must show the current row, every gate and light, old and next Q, phase enables and complete 12-tick ledger. Ledger bit words use the visible heading order, or equivalently labeled values. The normalized stage is a 300 by 96 logical light bank with three lamp centers at (50,48),(150,48),(250,48), radii 22, ordered Flare/Wash/Pearl. An on lamp uses that edition's supplied color, off is #182334. Keep the center disk solid; labels may be outside it. The stage can be resized or reframed; logical proportions stay intact. Waveform rows cover all 12 ticks and must update with edits; no static report or fake light label substitutes for actual colored preview. The three sheets and this guide remain available before repair.
The timing card is a separate six-frame bench example with zero initial Q; it is not either edition's full answer. Use it to check initial-tick and simultaneous-commit ordering. Two delivered editions share the illustrated topology but vary inputs, memories, colors and tempo. No hidden transition rules or attachment formats are required.
